title: This new AI trading platform is gaining momentum... thoughts?
author: Cute-Opposite4751
selftext:
Just sharing...

I stumbled upon this news about Perpetuals.com which is a huge company (listed on NASDAQ) that own a company called UpsideOnly. In short, this news talks about UpsideOnly which is a paper-trading/ai trading platform in which you practice with virtual capital and if your insights help their AI make successful trades, then you get up to 50% of the profits made. It's a cool model because they're looking for users to give them their market insights in exchange for the company's capital. So, in practice the trades are never done with your personal money, which is why they say its risk free. 

All in all, this article mentions how UpsideOnly's AI has performed, which proves the model is very effective and the company is getting lots of traction. They launched back in May and now they're already above 200K users, so something must be working on their end.

Anyways. Would love to know your thoughts on this, cuz it's making me curious. Have you heard or tried UpsideOnly? 

Here's the link in case you want to check the full news on Investing.com:

 https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/perpetuals-reports-380-return-in-ai-trading-backtest-93CH-4841835

Cheers and trade safe!

comments.author: Interesting_Gold_792
comments.body:
This is an interesting model, especially the part where paper trading becomes a signal-discovery layer rather than just a simulator.  
The 380% backtest is obviously the part that grabs attention, but what I’d really like to see is the forward/live validation.  
If the system is selecting traders or signals from a large population, I’d be curious how they protect against selection bias. With enough users, somebody will always look exceptional over a short window purely by chance.  
For me the interesting question isn’t “who made the most money?” but “whose edge continues to survive out-of-sample after fees, execution and changing market regimes?”  
If they can demonstrate that consistently, the human-signal + AI-filter + company-capital model becomes much more interesting.
